How is a change reviewed in this repository?

says: Two people on one installation work in the same repository, work, and each binds its checkout (repository.bind). The first founds Team A and the second founds Team B (team.found). Three sources are registered and committed (source.home.register, source.revision.commit). Repository notes are homed in the repository, private, applying only to service billing. Team A's rate table is homed in Team A and applies more broadly, to jurisdiction KR across that Team's work. Team B's review rules are authored in a directory of this same repository, homed in Team B, and state applicability to repository work. The first person asks a question of the repository notes and one of Team A's table (knowledge.question.ask). Each view must come back from its own home, the repository notes under its narrow applicability and Team A's table under its broader one; the broader label does not become the repository's constraint, and the repository's does not become the Team's. The second person projects Team B's rules (role.project), and they come back to Team B's own member. When the first person asks for the same Team B rules (role.project), the answer must be refused with source_not_authorized, even though the bytes sit in the same repository and the rules name it. That person then opens a recipient link for a conversation in this repository's work (recipient.link.open) and asks to read Team B's rules for it (reader.body.read with that recipient). The answer must be denied with access_not_established, naming no source, unit or frontier. No body reaches that recipient, and the recipient does not gain access to Team B's source.
